title: Chapter 178: The Chase
html:
Black snow seemed to drift through the corridor. Zhang Ya stood amid the falling darkness, her hair absorbing energy from the dismembered monsters while the red of her dress burned brighter still.

She has gotten even stronger…

Chen Ge’s eye twitched. Zhang Ya’s affection for him was rising at a terrifying rate. What if it crossed some invisible threshold and she “accidentally” killed him?

Despite her sweet, quiet appearance, the girl had a fondness for tormenting her victims. If the story needed a candidate for its worst villain, she would be an excellent choice.

“We should leave the Third Sick Hall as soon as possible.” Chen Ge approached Zhang Ya, hoping to persuade her to go. Only the blinded creature remained of the three monsters. It was grievously wounded, and the faces covering its body screamed for help. Even Chen Ge could not help pitying it. “Zhang Ya, it’s suffered enough. Stop torturing it and finish it off. We’re in a hurry, and I have no intention of staying here any longer than necessary.”

Blood poured like tears from the monster’s remaining eye. It thrashed against the black hair binding it, and the faces on its body began to shriek.

“It’s calling for help? Then leave it and let’s go!” Chen Ge took several steps before realizing Zhang Ya had not moved. Her black hair slowly coiled around the monster’s legs. At the far end of the corridor, countless pulsing blood vessels stretched toward the creature and burrowed into its body, as though trying to rescue it.

The stench grew stronger. While Zhang Ya fought the blood vessels, the Third Sick Hall’s true monster was awakening. More vessels pushed from the walls and ceiling. Some wrapped around the creature’s upper body; the rest snaked toward Zhang Ya.

What’s controlling those blood vessels?Chen Ge moved to help Zhang Ya, but before he could reach her, the lanky monster tore in half. The vessels seized most of its body and dragged the pieces downstairs, leaving Zhang Ya with only a small portion.

It was the first time Chen Ge had seen Zhang Ya lose a contest, but as far as he was concerned, they were fortunate simply to be alive. He opened his mouth to urge her away. Before he could speak, black hair erupted from her back in waves, and the streak of red shot down the stairs.

Blood vessels ripped apart in her wake. Zhang Ya soon vanished from the fourth-floor corridor. A cold draft blew into Chen Ge’s open mouth. Two seconds later, he murmured, “She’s actually chasing it?”

He stared into the dark corridor as one horrifying possibility after another crowded his mind. Reason told him to leave. The situation had already spiraled far beyond his expectations, and retreat was the sensible choice. Yet Zhang Ya had gone on alone—and she might be lured through the blood-red door.

The world beyond that door was treacherous, and Zhang Ya could be outnumbered there. The more Chen Ge considered it, the more frightened he became. He struck the wall with his cleaver and shouted, “What am I doing?”

Then he clenched his teeth and sprinted into the darkness. Beside a swollen mattress, the white cat watched in confusion. The man said one thing and did another; he was even running faster than before.

Chen Ge raced from the fourth floor to the second without finding Zhang Ya. More bloodstains had appeared on the walls, lending the halls an even more ominous appearance.

“She destroyed every blood vessel on the third and fourth floors, but only some of them here. She must have stopped on this level.” When he still found no sign of Zhang Ya on the second floor, Chen Ge descended to the first.

The blood-red corridor stood empty. Chen Ge entered cautiously. “Don’t tell me… Zhang Ya already went through the blood-red door?”

He reached Room 3 and found its formerly closed door wide open. Someone had clearly passed through it. Chen Ge picked up the Doctor Skull-cracker’s hammer from the floor, then glanced into his backpack. The rooster was dead; it had perished without making a sound.

“Should I wait here or go in after her?” Silence lay beyond the door, and Chen Ge hesitated. He might not be able to survive the dangers inside, but if anything happened to Zhang Ya, remaining outside would not save him either.

His fingers trembled around the doorknob. Drawing a deep breath, he took the nearly shattered ballpoint pen from his pocket.

“It’s a new day, so I want to use my fortune-telling chance.” Chen Ge held the pen upright over the brown mattress. “Pen Spirit, is there any way to save both Zhang Ya and me?”

Without the slightest hesitation, the Pen Spirit wrote three words on the mattress: Enter the Door.

“Wasn’t that a little fast? Don’t you need to think about it?” Chen Ge pocketed the pen. After one last look at the door, he made his decision. His phone had little power left, but he called Men Nan. “You said mysterious memories sometimes surface in your mind. Do any of them take place in a blood-red world?”

“There are.”

“Focus on those memories. Is there anything I should watch for in that blood-red world?” Chen Ge could not abandon Zhang Ya. He was already in too deep, and he would need her help in the future. He could not afford to lose her.

“Very few of those memories involve the color red, and when they do, they all seem to occur in the same place.” Men Nan thought for a moment. “It’s a sealed room with no windows and only one door. The space is cramped, with a wooden bed, restraints attached to its frame, and machines beside it. It looks like an electroconvulsive-therapy room.”

“Electroshock therapy?”

“Yes. In the memory, several monsters entered that room. They tightened the restraints around the bed, then spoke among themselves. I think they were saying, ‘Don’t wake it.’” Recalling the scene seemed to increase the pressure in Men Nan’s head, and pain entered his voice. “I couldn’t see them clearly, but one seemed to have a disfigured face. I also heard a name—I think it was… Wu Fei.”

The disfigured man and Wu Fei were both patients from the Third Sick Hall, housed in Rooms 10 and 9 respectively. They were the most dangerous presences in the hospital.

“Is there anything else?” Chen Ge stood at the door.

“One thing, though I don’t know whether it will help. Ten years ago, the original personality told me that if I ever needed to find him, I must not speak after passing through the blood-red door.”

“All right, thank you.” Chen Ge sealed his lips, pocketed the phone, took up the hammer and cleaver, and stepped through the door.
